intro_html: Cuban picadillo is a beautiful mix of savory and sweet, with olives and golden raisins playing off cumin-spiced beef. It browns and simmers in one skillet, then goes over rice for an easy meal-prep bowl. This one runs around $5.00 a serving (at everyday cost) with 42 grams of protein and makes 14 bowls.
cost_closing_html: About $5.00 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 servings gives you 42 grams of protein at 565 calories.
upsell_html: Sweet, salty, savory, and cheap all at once, this bowl earns a permanent spot in the rotation. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: The olives and raisins are what make picadillo special for very little money. A single jar of olives and one bag of raisins carry the whole batch.
Store-brand tomato sauce works perfectly here. Buy the cheapest canned tomato sauce and save the difference.
Green peppers are cheapest in bulk. Buy peppers by the multi-pack when your store offers it.
make_it: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet, breaking it up, then drain the grease.
Add the chopped onion, green pepper, and garlic and cook until softened.
Stir in the tomato sauce, cumin, olives, and golden raisins.
Simmer for 15 to 20 minutes so the flavors come together.
Cook the rice while the picadillo simmers.
Spoon the beef over rice and serve.
